pico.outcome: Co-equal primary outcomes: (1) Composite MACE = first MI, ischemic/hemorrhagic stroke, HF hospitalization (inpatient visit_occurrence required), or all-cause death; (2) Incident CKD (first dx_ckd after index with no prior CKD code).
pico.comparator: 1:1 propensity-score-matched normotensive cohort from the same source (>=3 BPs in the same 24-mo window, all SBP <= 130 AND DBP <= 80, identical exclusions). Matched on age (+/-2yr), sex, race, calendar quarter of index. Sensitivity: greedy 1:1.
pico.population: Adults aged 18+ with two consecutive elevated office BPs (SBP >= 130 OR DBP >= 80, ACC/AHA 2017) on distinct calendar days within a 24-month window; >=365 days of prior observation; no prior cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease, secondary hypertension, or antihypertensive exposure.
pico.intervention: Diagnostic latency: time from the second consecutive elevated BP (index date) to first recorded HTN diagnosis, stratified by tertile cutoffs at 6 and 12 months; sensitivity at the Lu 2025 16-month cutoff.
pico.time_at_risk: Index through earliest of: 5-year follow-up (primary), end of observation, death (for non-death outcomes), or last available follow-up (sensitivity). Symmetric censoring T vs C.

intent_json.hypothesis: Patients with a recorded hypertension diagnosis more than 12 months after their second consecutive elevated office BP measurement experience higher incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MI, ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, heart failure hospitalization, all-cause death) and incident chronic kidney disease compared to (a) patients with timely diagnosis and (b) a propensity-matched normotensive comparator.
known_gaps: BP threshold operator: protocol v3 used strict >; v3.1 corrected to >= per AHA 2017 - pending Dr. Bock final confirmation.
Lu 2025 exact citation (DOI/PMID) - referenced as ref 5 in v3 protocol; incomplete.
Antihypertensive scope: RxNorm class C02-C09 - pending Dr. Bock confirmation that Lu 2025 used same scope.
Resistant-HTN definition: apparent treatment-resistant (>=3 classes overlapping >=30d) without enforcing diuretic inclusion - labeled apparent, not AHA-canonical resistant.
HF outcome qualification: inpatient visit_occurrence required for MACE composite inclusion.
Cost analysis (Goal g) feasibility depends on OMOP cost table fidelity for the Acumenus source.
Renal sympathetic denervation procedure codes pre-2018 (0338T/0339T deleted) - pre-2018 alternates not catalogued.
Treatment-naive lookback: ever-before-index used primary; 12-month lookback sensitivity.
risk_notes: PHI/HIPAA: Acumenus OMOP CDM uses pseudonymized person_id; no MRNs or direct identifiers persisted in study outputs.
Residual confounding from EHR data quality - mitigated via empirical calibration on OHDSI negative-control outcomes.
Incomplete death capture in OMOP death table - sensitivity analysis excluding death from MACE composite.
BP measurement context (office vs ED vs inpatient) not always recorded - filter via visit_concept_id.

lu_reference.claim: Median diagnostic delay 16-18 months; 29% higher CV risk score when delay > 1 year

open_questions.default: exclude baseline CKD primary; covariate sensitivity
demote to encounter-counts if cost sparse

intent_json.study_title_alt: Failure of Hypertension Interventions in a Large Study Population (V3)
intent_json.primary_objective: Quantify the association between diagnostic latency in incident hypertension and downstream MACE plus incident CKD, and reproduce Lu et al. 2025's reported 29% higher cardiovascular risk score for patients with diagnostic delay > 12 months.
intent_json.research_question: Among adults aged 18 years and older with two consecutive elevated office blood pressure measurements (SBP >= 130 mmHg OR DBP >= 80 mmHg per ACC/AHA 2017) within a 24-month window and no prior cardiovascular disease, chronic kidney disease, thyroid disease, secondary hypertension, or antihypertensive exposure, does the latency from first elevated blood pressure to recorded hypertension diagnosis predict major adverse cardiovascular events (myocardial infarction, ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke, heart failure hospitalization, or all-cause death) and incident chronic kidney disease compared to a propensity-matched normotensive comparator? Secondary aims: (a) reproduce Lu 2025's reported 29 percent higher cardiovascular risk score among patients with diagnostic delay greater than 12 months; (b) characterize antihypertensive treatment trajectories; (c) describe apparent treatment-resistant hypertension class composition and renal-sympathetic-denervation eligibility; (d) measure baseline laboratory ordering frequency including CBC, CMP, lipid panel, TSH, and serum aldosterone.
intent_json.scientific_rationale: Diagnostic delay in hypertension is hypothesized to allow subclinical end-organ damage to accrue before treatment, raising long-term cardiovascular and renal risk. Lu et al. 2025 reported a median diagnostic delay of 16-18 months and a 29% higher cardiovascular risk score in delayed-diagnosis patients. This study reproduces that finding on the Acumenus OMOP CDM (~1M adults) and extends it with: co-equal CKD outcome; two-component latency decomposition (first-elevated to second-elevated, and second-elevated to recorded diagnosis); apparent treatment-resistant hypertension class composition; renal-sympathetic-denervation eligibility; baseline lab ordering including serum aldosterone.
